questions.evidence:
Report chat: A search result says the town clock was built in 1890. I have copied that year onto our slide. The result title looks official, but I have not opened the page yet. It might save time if we use the short summary.

Editor: Open the page before relying on it. The year may refer to a renovation rather than the first construction. Check the sentence around the number and identify who published the information. We need a source that actually supports our specific statement.

Writer: The page says the clock was repaired in 1890 and first installed in 1872. The summary left out that distinction. I will change the slide to 1872 for installation and keep 1890 only in the repair timeline.

Editor: Good. Add the source title and link to our notes, then check the other copied dates too. A convenient summary can help locate material, but it should not silently replace reading the evidence behind a claim.
